missions.name: Lunar Relay
briefing: Put a relay orbiter around the Moon. It has to stay, not fly past.
Launch from 200 km Earth orbit. Raise apoapsis to lunar distance, then capture at closest approach.
hints: Lunar capture at periapsis: roughly 600 m/s retrograde.

objectives.label: Stable lunar orbit
objectives.detail: Bound orbit inside the Moon's SOI.

objectives.label: Relay science packet
objectives.detail: Transmit within 30,000 km of the Moon.

missions.science_note: The Moon is tidally locked, so one hemisphere never faces Earth. A high lunar relay orbit keeps both the near side and the far side in contact with mission control.

missions.name: Jezero Descent
briefing: Land a 1,025 kg rover in Jezero Crater.
Wait for an Earth-Mars window. Fit the ablative shield before arrival.
Mars gets 43% of Earth's sunlight. Plan power for that.
hints: Trans-Mars injection: about 3.6 km/s from low Earth orbit.
Mars capture: 1.5 to 2.0 km/s retrograde at periapsis.
Atmosphere entry ends the mission. Heat shield required.

objectives.label: Survive entry
objectives.detail: Reach the atmosphere with a heat shield.

missions.science_note: Mars has less than 1% of Earth's atmospheric pressure. A lander needs a heat shield, a parachute and retro-rockets, each doing part of the braking.

missions.name: Metal World
briefing: Rendezvous with 16 Psyche and map its magnetic field.
2.9 AU out. Solar output is under a tenth of Earth's.
Ion drive: high Isp, low thrust. Long spirals.
hints: RTGs beat solar past the asteroid belt.
Spiral out with many small burns.
missions.science_note: 16 Psyche may be the exposed metallic core of a shattered protoplanet. Its density and radar brightness point to iron and nickel rather than rock.

missions.name: Europa Clipper
briefing: Five close flybys of Europa, inside Jupiter's radiation belts.
5.2 AU: solar is dead weight. Bring RTGs.
Aim perijove to thread Europa's orbit.
hints: Jupiter arrival: about 6.3 km/s from low Earth orbit.
Fast flybys and hardened cores keep the electronics alive.
missions.science_note: Europa's ice shell probably hides a salty ocean. Jupiter's tides flex the moon and supply the heat that keeps the water liquid.

missions.name: Outer Grand Tour
briefing: Jupiter flyby, Saturn capture, probe release at Titan.
Gravity assists are the only affordable route.
9.5 AU: RTGs mandatory, solar dead weight.
hints: Use Jupiter to bend the trajectory outward.
Saturn capture: retrograde burn inside its SOI.
Two RTGs keep the bus alive.

objectives.label: Saturn orbit
objectives.detail: Bound orbit inside the Saturn SOI.

missions.science_note: A gravity assist borrows orbital energy from a planet. Voyager used Jupiter and Saturn to reach the outer solar system with very little propellant.

missions.name: Landing Drill
briefing: Landing drill. You start 2 km above the Moon with no horizontal velocity.
Gravity is already pulling you down. Watch SURFACE ALTITUDE and RELATIVE SPEED.
Touch down under 40 m/s. END files the report.
hints: Warp until SURFACE ALTITUDE is under 1 km, then pause.
Burn retrograde. Keep RELATIVE SPEED below 40 m/s at touchdown.
This drill is about the final brake, not the transfer.
missions.science_note: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no parachute or aerobraking. Every metre per second of landing speed has to come from the engine.
